chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Running the Alabam: Brownskin Models and the busiest nights
summary: Their eight or nine months included the Brownskin Models and local entertainers, with Thursday, Saturday and Sunday the only good nights.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So how long did you and he operate the Alabam?
Oh, eight or nine months, I guess. Didn't last long.
And whom did you have in there when you were running it?

Well, the one thing we had in there was the Brownskin Models for awhile. They came through here. That was Miller's brother, you know. You know who Miller was? Had the...uh...what was the big Negro show they had back, so big? "Runnin' Wild" and "Shuffle Along"...yeah, Miller, and his brother had the Brownskin Models, and

they travelled all over, and they had a nice show. And we had them in there six or eight weeks, you know, did different shows, and we had all the local entertainers in there, you know. [Flournay Miller]
Who? Which ones of the local entertainers?
I don't remember any of them now, it's been so long. They come and go, you know.
Did you have a house band?
I know we had a white boy in there--a female impersonator. He was pretty good. He was in there for awhile. Come in with his big furs and things on, and he sing. Fur coats.
And the clientele at the Alabam was both black and white. Right?

Well, after Mosby left, see, it was so uncertain, they didn't have many white people come down there. And we had big Saturday nights, big Thursday nights and big Sunday nights, and that was about all. See, Thursday night, you know, has always been a big night when all the cooks and things are off, and that's when all the dances were, and then Saturday night, and Sundays. The rest of the nights are just...you know--make expenses you're lucky. See? So that's the way it is. I don't know how it is now.
